arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Bilderback argued that federal habeas relief is unavailable unless the state court decision was unreasonable.
Justice Sotomayor questioned whether the defense attorney’s lack of preparation was the only new fact.
Justice Sotomayor asked if the attorney’s trial statement proved he did not expect a mitigation hearing.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal habeas review. It asks if federal courts must reweigh evidence or accept state court conclusions.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants federal courts to reweigh evidence and grant habeas relief.
the opposing side wants federal courts to defer to state court findings and deny relief.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the power of federal courts to review state criminal convictions. It determines how much weight federal judges give to state court evidence. The outcome shapes the balance between federal oversight and state judicial authority.
